{
  "project_id": "P-KHM-BasicEducationImprovement",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Overloaded financial management staff may cause delays in processing transactions and reporting, slowing project execution.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Recruit additional FM officers, provide capacity‑building, and set clear processing timelines.",
      "evidence": "FM assessment notes staff may be overloaded, potentially leading to delays in processing transactions and reporting (page 63)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Delayed approval of the Annual Work Plan and Budget could postpone implementation of key activities.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Prepare draft AWPB early, secure inter‑ministerial sign‑off, and monitor approval milestones.",
      "evidence": "Delayed approval of the Annual Work Plan and Budget may hinder timely implementation (page 63)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "School mentoring funds may not be adequately monitored, risking misallocation or ineffective use.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Implement a robust school‑level monitoring system, regular audits, and transparent reporting of mentoring expenditures.",
      "evidence": "Risk that school mentoring funding may not be properly monitored (page 63)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "MoEYS procurement personnel lack sufficient knowledge of World Bank procurement rules, risking delays and non‑compliance.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Assign a full‑time procurement officer and deliver targeted World Bank procurement training to staff.",
      "evidence": "MoEYS staff’s limited knowledge and experience with World Bank Procurement Regulations (page 68)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Potential corruption in procurement processes could undermine project integrity and increase costs.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Publish procurement plans, establish a complaint mechanism, and conduct independent oversight audits.",
      "evidence": "Governance risks, including corrupt practices in procurement (page 68)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Frequent floods, cyclones and extreme heat threaten school infrastructure and cause prolonged closures.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Apply climate‑resilient design, elevate foundations, install flood‑proof features, and activate CERC when needed.",
      "evidence": "Natural disasters... floods, cyclones, extreme heat... lead to prolonged school closures (page 12)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Insufficient teacher capacity to adopt EGL and TaRL methods may limit learning gains.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Scale CPD, mentoring, and on‑site coaching; use phased rollout with competency assessments.",
      "evidence": "Insufficient teacher capacity noted as a principal cause of poor outcomes (page 7)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Overcrowded classrooms (>30 students) reduce individual attention and hinder learning outcomes.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Prioritize construction of additional classrooms in high‑density schools using the $36 M subcomponent.",
      "evidence": "76 % of primary students learn in classes with >30 students; reducing large classes improves learning (page 37)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Limited access to quality early childhood education reduces school readiness of incoming pupils.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Build 60 childcare centers and 60 ECE classes, provide teacher training, and run community awareness campaigns.",
      "evidence": "Limited readiness among children due to inadequate access to quality childcare and ECE services (page 7)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Inadequate data and awareness on gender‑based violence in schools hampers prevention and response.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Integrate GBV training for teachers, strengthen GRM, and collect gender‑disaggregated incident data.",
      "evidence": "Significant lack of comprehensive data on GBV prevalence; GEIP includes GBV TA team (page 57)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "New school buildings may not fully comply with universal design, limiting accessibility for children with disabilities.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Mandate universal design standards in all construction contracts and conduct third‑party accessibility audits.",
      "evidence": "New school buildings must adhere to universal design principles, including ramps and accessible toilets (page 59)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Donor‑funded EGL components are set to phase out by 2027, risking sustainability of interventions.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Develop a government financing plan to absorb EGL costs and seek additional development partner contributions.",
      "evidence": "DPs support expected to phase out by 2027 (page 21)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Targeted instruction pilot (TaRL) lacks robust evidence for large‑scale rollout, risking ineffective scaling.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Conduct rigorous impact evaluation of the pilot, refine methodology, and adopt an implementation‑learning agenda before scaling.",
      "evidence": "Targeted instruction only piloted in 2025, implying limited information for scale (page 36)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "ICT equipment may fail under extreme heat and humidity, disrupting digital learning.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Procure climate‑rated ICT hardware, provide climate‑controlled storage, and establish maintenance contracts.",
      "evidence": "Selecting ICT equipment designed to withstand extreme temperatures and humidity (page 62)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R15",
      "description": "HRMIS modernization could face technical delays and low staff adoption, limiting HR data quality.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Phase HRMIS rollout, provide user training, and monitor usage metrics to ensure adoption.",
      "evidence": "Modernizing HRMIS; Phase 2 conditional on technical feasibility (page 40)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R16",
      "description": "CERC manual development may be delayed, reducing ability to mobilize emergency financing quickly.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Assign a dedicated team with a fixed timeline to draft and approve the CERC manual before project mid‑term.",
      "evidence": "Project will develop a manual for CERC to ensure activation at any time (page 45)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R17",
      "description": "Insufficient stakeholder and community engagement could lead to low ownership and implementation resistance.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Maintain an active GRM, conduct regular citizen surveys, and hold community consultation workshops.",
      "evidence": "Project will actively involve citizens through extensive consultations and GRM (page 60)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R18",
      "description": "Early Learning Partnership grant closing in 2027 may not align with project timelines, creating funding gaps.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Coordinate with ELP trustees to align disbursement schedule and explore supplementary financing sources.",
      "evidence": "Trust Fund closing date differs; scheduled to close on April 30 2027 (page 22)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R19",
      "description": "Weak data quality in monitoring and evaluation could impair tracking of learning outcomes.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Strengthen PMU data collection capacity, use third‑party verification, and conduct periodic data quality audits.",
      "evidence": "M&E activities will be conducted by the PMU using government data, surveys, and reports (page 50)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R20",
      "description": "Construction may not meet climate‑resilient standards, reducing building durability during disasters.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Enforce climate‑resilient construction guidelines, conduct independent inspections, and require compliance certificates.",
      "evidence": "Climate‑resilient construction includes elevated foundations, energy‑efficient systems (page 61)."
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Overloaded financial management staff may cause delays in processing transactions and reporting, slowing project execution.
risks.mitigation: Recruit additional FM officers, provide capacity‑building, and set clear processing timelines.
risks.evidence: FM assessment notes staff may be overloaded, potentially leading to delays in processing transactions and reporting (page 63).

risks.description: Delayed approval of the Annual Work Plan and Budget could postpone implementation of key activities.
risks.mitigation: Prepare draft AWPB early, secure inter‑ministerial sign‑off, and monitor approval milestones.
risks.evidence: Delayed approval of the Annual Work Plan and Budget may hinder timely implementation (page 63).

risks.description: School mentoring funds may not be adequately monitored, risking misallocation or ineffective use.
risks.mitigation: Implement a robust school‑level monitoring system, regular audits, and transparent reporting of mentoring expenditures.
risks.evidence: Risk that school mentoring funding may not be properly monitored (page 63).

risks.description: MoEYS procurement personnel lack sufficient knowledge of World Bank procurement rules, risking delays and non‑compliance.
risks.mitigation: Assign a full‑time procurement officer and deliver targeted World Bank procurement training to staff.
risks.evidence: MoEYS staff’s limited knowledge and experience with World Bank Procurement Regulations (page 68).

risks.description: Potential corruption in procurement processes could undermine project integrity and increase costs.
risks.mitigation: Publish procurement plans, establish a complaint mechanism, and conduct independent oversight audits.
risks.evidence: Governance risks, including corrupt practices in procurement (page 68).

risks.description: Frequent floods, cyclones and extreme heat threaten school infrastructure and cause prolonged closures.
risks.mitigation: Apply climate‑resilient design, elevate foundations, install flood‑proof features, and activate CERC when needed.
risks.evidence: Natural disasters... floods, cyclones, extreme heat... lead to prolonged school closures (page 12).

risks.description: Insufficient teacher capacity to adopt EGL and TaRL methods may limit learning gains.
risks.mitigation: Scale CPD, mentoring, and on‑site coaching; use phased rollout with competency assessments.
risks.evidence: Insufficient teacher capacity noted as a principal cause of poor outcomes (page 7).

risks.description: Overcrowded classrooms (>30 students) reduce individual attention and hinder learning outcomes.
risks.mitigation: Prioritize construction of additional classrooms in high‑density schools using the $36 M subcomponent.
risks.evidence: 76 % of primary students learn in classes with >30 students; reducing large classes improves learning (page 37).

risks.description: Limited access to quality early childhood education reduces school readiness of incoming pupils.
risks.mitigation: Build 60 childcare centers and 60 ECE classes, provide teacher training, and run community awareness campaigns.
risks.evidence: Limited readiness among children due to inadequate access to quality childcare and ECE services (page 7).

risks.description: Inadequate data and awareness on gender‑based violence in schools hampers prevention and response.
risks.mitigation: Integrate GBV training for teachers, strengthen GRM, and collect gender‑disaggregated incident data.
risks.evidence: Significant lack of comprehensive data on GBV prevalence; GEIP includes GBV TA team (page 57).

risks.description: New school buildings may not fully comply with universal design, limiting accessibility for children with disabilities.
risks.mitigation: Mandate universal design standards in all construction contracts and conduct third‑party accessibility audits.
risks.evidence: New school buildings must adhere to universal design principles, including ramps and accessible toilets (page 59).

risks.description: Donor‑funded EGL components are set to phase out by 2027, risking sustainability of interventions.
risks.mitigation: Develop a government financing plan to absorb EGL costs and seek additional development partner contributions.
risks.evidence: DPs support expected to phase out by 2027 (page 21).

risks.description: Targeted instruction pilot (TaRL) lacks robust evidence for large‑scale rollout, risking ineffective scaling.
risks.mitigation: Conduct rigorous impact evaluation of the pilot, refine methodology, and adopt an implementation‑learning agenda before scaling.
risks.evidence: Targeted instruction only piloted in 2025, implying limited information for scale (page 36).

risks.description: ICT equipment may fail under extreme heat and humidity, disrupting digital learning.
risks.mitigation: Procure climate‑rated ICT hardware, provide climate‑controlled storage, and establish maintenance contracts.
risks.evidence: Selecting ICT equipment designed to withstand extreme temperatures and humidity (page 62).

risks.description: HRMIS modernization could face technical delays and low staff adoption, limiting HR data quality.
risks.mitigation: Phase HRMIS rollout, provide user training, and monitor usage metrics to ensure adoption.
risks.evidence: Modernizing HRMIS; Phase 2 conditional on technical feasibility (page 40).

risks.description: CERC manual development may be delayed, reducing ability to mobilize emergency financing quickly.
risks.mitigation: Assign a dedicated team with a fixed timeline to draft and approve the CERC manual before project mid‑term.
risks.evidence: Project will develop a manual for CERC to ensure activation at any time (page 45).

risks.description: Insufficient stakeholder and community engagement could lead to low ownership and implementation resistance.
risks.mitigation: Maintain an active GRM, conduct regular citizen surveys, and hold community consultation workshops.
risks.evidence: Project will actively involve citizens through extensive consultations and GRM (page 60).

risks.description: Early Learning Partnership grant closing in 2027 may not align with project timelines, creating funding gaps.
risks.mitigation: Coordinate with ELP trustees to align disbursement schedule and explore supplementary financing sources.
risks.evidence: Trust Fund closing date differs; scheduled to close on April 30 2027 (page 22).

risks.description: Weak data quality in monitoring and evaluation could impair tracking of learning outcomes.
risks.mitigation: Strengthen PMU data collection capacity, use third‑party verification, and conduct periodic data quality audits.
risks.evidence: M&E activities will be conducted by the PMU using government data, surveys, and reports (page 50).

risks.description: Construction may not meet climate‑resilient standards, reducing building durability during disasters.
risks.mitigation: Enforce climate‑resilient construction guidelines, conduct independent inspections, and require compliance certificates.
risks.evidence: Climate‑resilient construction includes elevated foundations, energy‑efficient systems (page 61).
